cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 16th District in the U.S. House since January 2025. Former San Jose mayor (2015–2022) and San Jose city councilmember (2007–2015). Earlier worked as a Santa Clara County prosecutor and a federal prosecutor. Harvard Law and Kennedy School graduate.

controversies.text: Liccardo didn't publicly disclose his joint interest in a downtown condo his wife owned before their 2013 marriage until 2018. He cast two votes in favor of the Google project. He apologized and told KQED, "I screwed up." The city attorney says the law finds no conflict beyond 500 feet. The condo was about a mile away.
Missed 9 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.3%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 2, 2026-04-27 to 2026-04-27.

In February 2017, Liccardo signed a nondisclosure agreement at Google's request, as did nearly 20 San Jose officials. Two nonprofits sued the city over secrecy. In 2019 a judge dismissed the suit. She ruled the city had handed over the documents it needed to. She did not rule on whether the agreements were proper.

cands.gaps: Neither source names his birthplace, so where he was born is unconfirmed. Sources differ on whether he grew up in San Jose or Saratoga; both are in California. We found no documented position for or against banning data centers; he says only that he is leading legislation to incentivize renewables and batteries for data centers. We found nothing on his stance toward homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, police pay and pensions, gun laws, school choice, or teacher pay. His 2014 pension-reform work covered all city employees, and the pages do not say how it affected police specifically. The Ballotpedia page was cut off, so its later sections were not read, and the campaign homepage gave little on policy.

Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Peter Sundin Soulé

money.note: Individuals gave $4,172; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $100. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 16th Congressional District in 2026. Holds a UCSB bachelor's degree and a Golden Gate University MBA in finance. Worked in the family business, Soule Steel, in property management, accounting and finance. Served on the San Jose Civil Service Commission 2007–2011.

endorsements.text: Per Ballotpedia, he received voter-guide recommendations from April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.
In his Ballotpedia survey he lists endorsements from the American Independent Party, the California Republican Assembly and the Silicon Valley Association of Conservative Republicans (self-reported).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Soule was born or raised, or when he came to California. His own site shows Bay Area activity since 2004 and a family business in San Francisco and Los Angeles. He has held no elected office, so there is no record of official actions to report. His stated positions are limited to his campaign website and Ballotpedia survey. We found nothing on his views about data centers, development and growth limits, homestead property taxes, abortion, campaign finance or police pay and pensions, and no documented controversies.

score.why: Raised $4,272, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
